title: Worksheet 7: Grace Hopper and the First "Bug"
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: Grace Hopper was an American computer scientist and U.S. Navy officer who made major contributions to early computer programming. In 1947, Hopper and her team were working on a computer called the Mark II when the machine suddenly stopped working correctly. When they investigated, they found an actual moth trapped inside one of the computer's electrical relays, causing the malfunction. The team removed the moth and taped it into their logbook, writing "First actual case of bug being found." While the term "bug" had been used before to describe technical problems, this event is one of the most famous early examples of the word being used this way, and it helped popularize the term "debugging" to describe the process of finding and fixing errors in a program. Grace Hopper also helped develop one of the first programming languages that used English-like words instead of numbers.
